speaker: gauge
text: This highway curve is tilted. I'll flatten it.

speaker: fitz
text:
Wait. That tilt is on purpose.
Turning takes a push toward the inside of the curve. On a level road, only tire grip gives that push.

speaker: fitz
text: The road leans in, so it pushes partly toward the inside too. The tires need less grip.

speaker: gauge
text: Then why not tilt it more?

speaker: fitz
text: On ice, a slow or stopped car could slide down the slope. So the tilt stays gentle.

speaker: gauge
text: Ooh, what else is built weird? Subscribe and let's find out.
